fields.label: Intro paragraph
fields.value: Tooth decay, small chips and worn areas can weaken teeth and cause sensitivity or discomfort. White fillings, also known as tooth-coloured or composite fillings, repair these areas using a material that is matched to the natural shade of your teeth.

fields.label: Intro paragraph
fields.value: At Precision Dental, we aim to detect decay early, when a small, conservative filling is often all that is needed.

fields.label: Heading
fields.value: What Are White Fillings?

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: White fillings are made from composite resin, a tooth-coloured material that is bonded directly to the tooth. The material is applied in layers, shaped to restore the natural contours of your tooth and hardened with a special curing light.

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: Because composite bonds to the tooth surface, it can often be placed with less removal of healthy tooth structure than some traditional filling materials. It can also be used to replace old amalgam fillings when they are worn, cracked or decayed.

fields.label: Heading
fields.value: Are White Fillings Right for You?

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: A white filling may be recommended if you have:

fields.label: List item
fields.value: A cavity caused by tooth decay

fields.label: List item
fields.value: A small chip or fracture

fields.label: List item
fields.value: Worn areas near the gum line

fields.label: List item
fields.value: A worn, leaking or broken older filling

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: Composite fillings are well suited to small and medium-sized restorations. If a large part of the tooth is missing or weakened, a crown, inlay or onlay may offer more protection, and options such as CEREC same-day crowns may be discussed.

fields.label: Heading
fields.value: What Happens at Your Appointment

fields.label: Subheading
fields.value: Diagnosis

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: Decay is often found during a routine check-up and clean. We use digital X-rays and DiagnoCam, which uses light to help identify decay between teeth and beneath fillings without radiation. We show you what we find and explain your options.

fields.label: Subheading
fields.value: Preparing the Tooth

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: Local anaesthetic is used to keep you comfortable. Decay and any old filling material are carefully removed, and the tooth is cleaned and prepared for bonding.

fields.label: Subheading
fields.value: Placing the Filling

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: Composite resin is applied in thin layers, each set with a curing light. The filling is then shaped, your bite is checked, and the surface is polished to a smooth finish.

fields.label: Heading
fields.value: Aftercare and Ongoing Care

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: Wait until the numbness has worn off before eating to avoid biting your cheek or tongue. Some sensitivity to hot and cold is normal for a short time. Brush twice daily with fluoride toothpaste, clean between your teeth, limit sugary foods and drinks, and attend regular check-ups. If your bite feels high or you notice persistent sensitivity, please contact us.

sections.label: Why Choose Precision Dental for White Fillings

fields.label: Heading
fields.value: Why Choose Precision Dental for White Fillings

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: We place great importance on early detection and conservative care. With digital X-rays, DiagnoCam and an intra-oral camera, we can identify concerns early and show you exactly what we are seeing, so you understand why treatment is recommended.

sections.label: Fees, Health Funds and Payment Options

fields.label: Heading
fields.value: Fees, Health Funds and Payment Options

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: The cost of your treatment depends on your individual needs. After your examination, we talk you through your options and the expected fees before any treatment begins. We accept most major health funds, process claims on the spot through HICAPS and are a preferred provider for {{site:preferredFunds}}. Payment plans are available through DentiCare for eligible patients, subject to terms and conditions. You can learn more on our Prices and Payment Options page.

fields.label: Small label
fields.value: FAQ

fields.label: Heading
fields.value: Frequently Asked Questions

fields.label: Question
fields.value: How long do white fillings last?

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: The lifespan of a filling depends on its size, location, your bite, grinding habits and oral hygiene. Regular check-ups help us monitor your fillings over time.

fields.label: Question
fields.value: Does getting a filling hurt?

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: Local anaesthetic is used so you are comfortable during treatment. You may feel some sensitivity afterwards, which usually settles within a few days.

fields.label: Question
fields.value: Should I replace my old silver fillings?

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: Amalgam fillings that are intact and not causing problems do not always need replacing. We recommend replacement when a filling is worn, cracked, leaking or has decay around it.

fields.label: Question
fields.value: Can I eat straight after a white filling?

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: Composite fillings are set with a curing light, so they are hard before you leave. We recommend waiting until the anaesthetic wears off before eating.

fields.label: Question
fields.value: Will my filling match my teeth?

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: We select a composite shade that blends with your surrounding teeth. Fillings will not change colour with whitening, so it is best to whiten beforehand if you plan to.

fields.label: Question
fields.value: What happens if I leave a cavity untreated?

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: Decay can progress deeper into the tooth, which may lead to a toothache, infection or the need for more involved treatment such as root canal therapy or a crown.
